title: The Immune System Explained I - Bacteria Infection
beats: You are under constant attack; the body fields an army with guards, intelligence, factories
Assume 12 jobs, 21 cells, 2 protein forces, each cell up to 4 jobs; assign them
Colour per job; cell icon centre main job, ring secondary; interaction map drawn
Admires complexity, then scopes down to only the cells needed
You cut yourself on a rusty nail; skin breached
Bacteria double every 20 minutes; quorum change in behavior
Macrophages as border guards, up to 100 each; inflammation
Messenger proteins call backup; neutrophils fight furiously, kill friends, suicide at 5 days
Dendritic cell as brain: samples enemy, presents pieces, decides virus vs bacteria forces
T-cell training, only a quarter survive; matching set-up
Activation cascade: duplication, memory cells, to battlefield, to B cell factory
Helper T cells keep factories alive then let them die
Antibodies named last: protein that binds the specific intruder
Second line of defense: antibodies disable, tag for macrophages; balance shifts
Admits this was very simplified; closes on complexity as beauty

metrics.examples: 1 running scenario (rusty nail) told once; cell roles reused by analogy
metrics.ending: Honest simplification caveat and an appeal to wonder

new_moves.name: full-map-then-filter
new_moves.what: Show whole complex system with colour code, then declare which part to follow

new_moves.name: chronological-narrative-as-order
new_moves.what: Time order of an infection used as the dependency order

theory: The video shows complexity honestly up front, then makes it legible with a one-time visual code and a single time-ordered story. Chronology serves as the dependency order, so each new cell enters exactly when the story needs it. Admitting the simplification at the end builds trust.
velocity: Scene builder: for systems with many actors, render the full map first, then highlight only the cast needed per scene
Orchestrator: use event chronology to sequence new terms; introduce each actor at the moment it acts
Learner model: cap new named entities per minute; this video exceeds it and is a negative example
Voice: end with an explicit what-we-left-out beat
